title: Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization (G.17, October 2026 data) — 9:15 a.m. ET, the only pre-open release on a four-release morning
source: FED: two independent federalreserve.gov primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06 — the Board's G.17 announcements feed (feeds/g17.html, HTTP 200, 614,006 bytes) states verbatim "In 2026, the G.17 release on Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization will be published at 9:15 a.m. on January 16, February 18, March 16, April 16, May 15, June 15, July 17, August 18, September 18, October 16, November 17, and December 16", and the Board's own release-date table (releases/g17/release_dates.htm, HTTP 200, 117,098 bytes) lists "November 2026 | 17-November-2026" in a run whose 2025 rows still read "October 2025 NA" and "November 2025 NA" from the funding lapse — i.e. the table is maintained, not stale. Corroborated a third time by the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx PostedUpdates sheet, whose 2026-11-17 row reads "Retail sales + inventories, Import and export prices, Industrial production". PROMOTED from the estimate filed by the mtis-2026-11-17 sweep: that lane could not self-confirm its own in-sweep discovery and said so, deferring promotion to this id's initial research, which is this session reading the Federal Reserve primaries directly. The Board's verb is "will be published", not the "anticipated" that keeps the Census siblings at estimate. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-06 by this event's own initial research, after reading the single proposal that existed for this id (proposals/industrial-production-2026-11-17.from-mtis-2026-11-17.json, now shadowed and inert). Every claim in that proposal was re-derived rather than carried; all survive, and one is sharpened against the proposer. The reference month is OCTOBER 2026 — month 1 of the quarter GDPNow is nowcasting from 2026-10-29 — which is the OPPOSITE position class from mtis-2026-11-17 on the same date and in the same GDPNow vintage, whose September reference month sits in the quarter before. Four releases share 2026-11-17 at three hours: Advance Monthly Retail Trade 08:30 (October data), import/export prices 08:30, this G.17 at 09:15 (October data), MTIS 10:00 (September data). This is the only one of the four that prints BEFORE the 09:30 cash open. Impact LOW and symbols empty on measured grounds, not by default: across 143 G.17 release dates carrying a GDPNow vintage, the report's own channel — the Equipment contribution — moves a median 0.0159pp while PCE moves 0.0852pp, and PCE outmoves Equipment on 124 of 143 (86.7%); strip the retail-sales co-release out and a G.17 vintage's GDP-nowcast move is statistically indistinguishable from an ordinary day (0.1033pp vs 0.0862pp, permutation p=0.342, n=84). On the tape, a G.17 release standing alone at 09:15 moves the overnight gap no more than an ordinary session (0.3109% vs 0.2786%, p=0.626, n=37, SPY 2014-05 onward). No house playbook is macro-keyed (grep of trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md re-run 2026-09-06, 0 hits) and no instrument attaches. The live open question is NOT the monthly number: the Board announced on 2026-05-15 that its ANNUAL REVISION — new 2022 base year, 2023 Census manufacturing benchmark, capacity through Q4-2025 — will land in the autumn of 2026, and as of 2026-09-06 it has no announced date. Date confirmed; nothing here licenses an entry.
